q: गुजरात का कौन-सा हड़प्पा स्थल पकी ईंटों से बने प्राचीन ज्वारीय गोदीवाड़ा (dockyard) के लिए प्रसिद्ध है?
e:
Lothal (on the Bhogava river, Gujarat, excavated by S. R. Rao in 1954) is renowned for the world's earliest known tidal dockyard and bead-making factory (लोथल प्राचीन गोदीवाड़ा के लिए प्रसिद्ध है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Kalibangan (Rajasthan, Ghaggar river) yielded ploughed field evidence and fire altars.
2. Dholavira (Gujarat, UNESCO site 2021) is famous for its three-part city layout and sophisticated water reservoirs.
3. Rakhigarhi (Haryana) is the largest Harappan site in India.
qe: Which Harappan site in Gujarat is famous for its ancient tidal dockyard made of baked bricks?

q: मध्य प्रदेश का कौन-सा पुरापाषाण/मध्यपाषाण पुरातात्विक स्थल अपने प्रागैतिहासिक शैलाश्रयों और गुफा चित्रों के लिए यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल के रूप में प्रसिद्ध है?
e:
Bhimbetka rock shelters (Raisen district, MP, discovered by V. S. Wakankar in 1957–58) preserve paintings spanning Palaeolithic to Mesolithic eras (भीमबेटका प्रागैतिहासिक शैलचित्रों के लिए प्रसिद्ध है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Burzahom (J&K, Neolithic) is known for pit-dwellings and dog burials with masters.
2. Mehrgarh (Balochistan) provides the earliest Neolithic evidence of agriculture (wheat/barley) in the Indian subcontinent.
3. Koldihwa and Lahuradewa (UP) provide early evidence of rice cultivation.
qe: Which Palaeolithic/Mesolithic archaeological site in Madhya Pradesh is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its prehistoric rock shelters and cave paintings?

q:
सूची-I (हड़प्पा स्थल) को सूची-II (नदी) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. हड़प्पा
2. मोहनजोदड़ो
3. आलमगीरपुर
4. मांडा
सूची-II:
(a) चिनाब
(b) हिंडन
(c) सिंधु
(d) रावी
e:
Harappa lies on Ravi, Mohenjo-daro on Indus, Alamgirpur (Meerut, UP — easternmost Harappan site) on Hindon, and Manda (J&K — northernmost site) on Chenab (1-d, 2-c, 3-b, 4-a)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Westernmost Harappan site: Sutkagendor (Dasht river, Balochistan); Southernmost: Daimabad (Pravara river, Maharashtra).
2. Harappa was excavated by Daya Ram Sahni (1921); Mohenjo-daro by R. D. Banerji (1922).
3. The famous bronze 'Dancing Girl' and 'Great Bath' were discovered at Mohenjo-daro.
qe:
Match List-I (Harappan Site) with List-II (River) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Harappa
2. Mohenjo-daro
3. Alamgirpur
4. Manda
List-II:
(a) Chenab
(b) Hindon
(c) Indus
(d) Ravi

q: सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता के लोगों को निम्नलिखित में से किस धातु का ज्ञान नहीं था?
e:
The Harappan Civilization was a Bronze Age (Chalcolithic/Urban) civilization; Iron (लोहा) appeared later in India during the Later Vedic / Painted Grey Ware (PGW) period (~1000 BCE) (हड़प्पावासी लोहे से अपरिचित थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Harappans procured copper from Khetri (Rajasthan) and Oman, tin from Afghanistan, and lapis lazuli from Badakhshan.
2. Harappan seals were mostly made of steatite (सेलखड़ी) featuring the unicorn bull and pictographic script (still undeciphered, boustrophedon style).
3. Chanhudaro is the only Harappan city without a citadel (दुर्ग).
qe: Which of the following metals was NOT known to the people of the Indus Valley Civilization?

q: शिकार-संग्रहण से स्थायी कृषि और पशुपालन की ओर संक्रमण को दर्शाने वाला 'नवपाषाण क्रांति' (Neolithic Revolution) शब्द किस पुरातत्वविद् ने गढ़ा था?
e:
Australian-British archaeologist V. Gordon Childe coined 'Neolithic Revolution' in 1936 (वी. गॉर्डन चाइल्ड ने नवपाषाण क्रांति शब्द दिया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Robert Bruce Foote ('Father of Indian Prehistory') discovered the first Palaeolithic hand-axe in India at Pallavaram (near Madras) in 1863.
2. Sir John Marshall was Director-General of ASI when Harappa and Mohenjo-daro were excavated in 1921–22.
3. Pottery, polished stone axes, and the wheel became widespread in the Neolithic Age.
qe: The term 'Neolithic Revolution' (नवपाषाण क्रांति), marking the transition from hunting-gathering to settled agriculture and domestication of animals, was coined by which archaeologist?

q: प्रसिद्ध 'गायत्री मंत्र' (सूर्य देव सवितृ को समर्पित) ऋग्वेद के किस मण्डल में संकलित है?
e:
The Gayatri Mantra (composed by Sage Vishwamitra) appears in the Third Mandala of the Rigveda (गायत्री मंत्र ऋग्वेद के तृतीय मण्डल में है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The Tenth Mandala contains the 'Purusha Sukta' (earliest mention of the four Varnas) and 'Nasadiya Sukta'.
2. The Seventh Mandala (Vasishtha) mentions the 'Battle of Ten Kings' (दशराज्ञ युद्ध) on the banks of Parushni (Ravi) river.
3. The Ninth Mandala is entirely dedicated to Soma.
qe: The famous 'Gayatri Mantra' (addressed to solar deity Savitr) is contained in which Mandala of the Rigveda?

q: युवा जिज्ञासु नचिकेता और यम (मृत्यु के देवता) के बीच आत्मा के स्वरूप पर प्रसिद्ध दार्शनिक संवाद किस उपनिषद में वर्णित है?
e:
The Yama–Nachiketa dialogue is the core of the Katha Upanishad (Krishna Yajurveda) (यम-नचिकेता संवाद कठोपनिषद में है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. 'Satyameva Jayate' (सत्यमेव जयते) is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.
2. 'Tamaso Ma Jyotirgamaya' and the Gargi–Yajnavalkya dialogue appear in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.
3. 'Aham Brahmasmi' is from Brihadaranyaka, while 'Tat Tvam Asi' is from Chandogya Upanishad.
qe: The ancient philosophical dialogue between the young seeker Nachiketa and Yama (Lord of Death) on the nature of the soul occurs in which Upanishad?

q: जैन धर्म के 23वें तीर्थंकर कौन थे, जिनका जन्म वाराणसी में हुआ था और जिन्होंने चार महाव्रतों (सत्य, अहिंसा, अस्तेय, अपरिग्रह) का उपदेश दिया?
e:
Parshvanatha (23rd Tirthankara, symbol: Serpent/Snake, son of King Ashvasena of Kashi) taught four vows; Mahavira (24th Tirthankara, symbol: Lion) added the 5th vow—Brahmacharya (पार्श्वनाथ 23वें तीर्थंकर थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Rishabhadeva (Adinatha, symbol: Bull) was the 1st Tirthankara.
2. First Jain Council: Pataliputra (~300 BCE, Sthulabhadra); Second Jain Council: Vallabhi, Gujarat (512 CE, Devardhi Kshamashramana).
3. Syadvada (Anekantavada — doctrine of manifold truth) is the core epistemology of Jainism.
qe: Who was the 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism, born in Varanasi, who preached four vows (Satya, Ahimsa, Asteya, Aparigraha)?

q: किस बौद्ध ग्रन्थ में ईसा पूर्व छठी शताब्दी के भारत के 'सोलह महाजनपदों' (षोडश महाजनपद) की सर्वप्रथम व्यवस्थित सूची मिलती है?
e:
The Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya (part of Sutta Pitaka) and the Jain text Bhagavati Sutra list the 16 Mahajanapadas (अंगुत्तर निकाय में सोलह महाजनपदों की सूची मिलती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Among the 16 Mahajanapadas, Asmaka (Assaka, on Godavari river) was the only one located in South India.
2. Vajji (capital Vaishali) and Malla (Kusinara/Pava) were prominent Gana-Sanghas (oligarchic republics).
3. Magadha (capitals: Rajagriha, later Pataliputra) emerged as the most powerful empire under Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, and the Nandas.
qe: Which Buddhist text provides the earliest systematic list of the 'Sixteen Mahajanapadas' (षोडश महाजनपद) of 6th-century BCE India?

q: किस बौद्ध संगीति के दौरान बौद्ध धर्म औपचारिक रूप से हीनयान और महायान सम्प्रदायों में विभाजित हुआ?
e:
The Hinayana–Mahayana split crystallized at the Fourth Buddhist Council (1st century CE, Kashmir, patronized by Kanishka, chaired by Vasumitra with Ashvaghosha as vice-president) (चतुर्थ बौद्ध संगीति में हीनयान व महायान विभाजन हुआ)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. First Council (483 BCE, Rajagriha, Ajatashatru, Mahakassapa): compilation of Sutta Pitaka (Ananda) & Vinaya Pitaka (Upali).
2. Second Council (383 BCE, Vaishali, Kalashoka, Sabakami): split into Sthaviravadins and Mahasanghikas.
3. Third Council (250 BCE, Pataliputra, Ashoka, Moggaliputta Tissa): compilation of Abhidhamma Pitaka.
qe: During which Buddhist Council did Buddhism formally split into the Hinayana (Theravada) and Mahayana sects?

q: सम्राट अशोक के किस वृहद शिलालेख में कलिंग युद्ध (261 ई.पू.) की विभीषिका और उसके बाद की धम्मविजय नीति का वर्णन मिलता है?
e:
Major Rock Edict XIII (13वाँ शिलालेख) vividly records the Kalinga War (8th regnal year of Ashoka) and mentions five contemporary Greek kings (तेरहवें शिलालेख में कलिंग युद्ध का वर्णन है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. James Prinsep first deciphered Ashoka's Brahmi script edicts in 1837.
2. Maski, Gujarra, Nettur, and Udegolam minor rock edicts explicitly mention the personal name 'Ashoka' (elsewhere he is 'Devanampiya Piyadassi').
3. Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts (Pakistan) are written in Kharosthi script (right to left).
qe: Which Major Rock Edict of Emperor Ashoka describes the horrors of the Kalinga War (261 BCE) and his subsequent policy of Dhammavijaya?

q: कौटिल्य के 'अर्थशास्त्र' में मौर्य राज्य के मुख्य राजस्व संग्राहक (कलेक्टर-जनरल) का आधिकारिक पदनाम क्या था?
e:
Samaharta was the Collector-General of Revenue, whereas Sannidhata was the Chief Treasurer / Custodian of the Royal Treasury (समाहर्ता मुख्य राजस्व अधिकारी तथा सन्निधाता कोषाध्यक्ष था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Sitadhyaksha supervised crown lands (Sita land); Panyadhyaksha regulated trade and commerce.
2. Megasthenes (ambassador of Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya) wrote 'Indica', describing Pataliputra's administration by 6 committees of 5 members each.
3. Kautilya's Saptanga Theory lists 7 elements of the state: Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda, and Mitra.
qe: In Kautilya's 'Arthashastra', what was the official designation of the chief revenue collector (collector-general) of the Mauryan state?

q: शुंग वंश का संस्थापक कौन था, जिसने 185 ई.पू. में अंतिम मौर्य शासक बृहद्रथ की हत्या की और दो अश्वमेध यज्ञ किए?
e:
Pushyamitra Shunga (commander-in-chief of Brihadratha) founded the Shunga dynasty; great grammarian Patanjali (author of 'Mahabhashya') was his contemporary and priest (पुष्यमित्र शुंग ने शुंग वंश की स्थापना की)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Agnimitra Shunga is the hero of Kalidasa's play 'Malavikagnimitram'.
2. Bharhut Stupa railings and Sanchi Stupa gateways (toranas) were embellished during the Shunga–Satavahana era.
3. Simuka founded the Satavahana dynasty in the Deccan (famous ruler: Gautamiputra Satakarni).
qe: Who was the founder of the Shunga dynasty, who assassinated the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha in 185 BCE and performed two Ashvamedha sacrifices?

q: प्रसिद्ध संस्कृत जूनागढ़ शिलालेख (150 ई.), जो विशुद्ध संस्कृत का प्रथम लंबा अभिलेख है और सुदर्शन झील के जीर्णोद्धार का वर्णन करता है, किस शक शासक ने उत्कीर्ण कराया था?
e:
Shaka Kshatrapa Rudradaman I issued the Junagadh inscription recording the repair of Sudarshana Lake (originally built by Pushyagupta under Chandragupta Maurya and later repaired by Skandagupta too) (जूनागढ़ अभिलेख रुद्रदामन प्रथम का है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Indo-Greek ruler Menander (Milinda) converted to Buddhism after philosophical dialogue with Nagasena, recorded in 'Milindapanha'.
2. Kushana ruler Kanishka started the Shaka Era in 78 CE (India's national calendar).
3. Gandhara School of Art (Greco-Buddhist, grey schist) and Mathura School (red sandstone) flourished under the Kushanas.
qe: The famous Sanskrit Junagadh Rock Inscription (150 CE), which is the earliest long inscription in chaste classical Sanskrit and records the repair of Sudarshana Lake, was issued by which Shaka ruler?

q: कुषाण सम्राट कनिष्क के प्रसिद्ध राजवैद्य कौन थे, जिन्होंने आयुर्वेद के आधारभूत ग्रन्थ 'चरक संहिता' की रचना की?
e:
Acharya Charaka ('Father of Indian Medicine') adorned Kanishka's court alongside Ashvaghosha ('Buddhacharita'), Nagarjuna (Madhyamika philosophy), and Vasumitra (चरक कनिष्क के राजवैद्य थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Sushruta ('Father of Surgery') authored 'Sushruta Samhita' detailing plastic surgery (rhinoplasty) and surgical instruments.
2. Dhanvantari was one of the Navaratnas (Nine Gems) at the court of Gupta Emperor Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).
3. The Kushanas were the first rulers in India to issue large-scale pure gold coins.
qe: Who was the famous court physician of Kushana Emperor Kanishka, author of the foundational Ayurvedic treatise 'Charaka Samhita'?

q: दरबारी कवि हरिषेण द्वारा संस्कृत चम्पू शैली में रचित 'प्रयाग प्रशस्ति' (इलाहाबाद स्तंभ लेख) किस गुप्त सम्राट की सैन्य विजयों का गुणगान करती है?
e:
Harishena's Prayaga Prashasti celebrates Samudragupta's campaigns in Aryavarta and Dakshinapatha; historian V. A. Smith called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India' (प्रयाग प्रशस्ति समुद्रगुप्त से संबंधित है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Samudragupta is depicted playing the Veena on his gold coins and held the title 'Kaviraja'.
2. The Mehrauli Iron Pillar (Delhi) is attributed to Chandragupta II ('Chandra').
3. Skandagupta's Bhitari Pillar Inscription (Ghazipur, UP) records his heroic victory over the Hunas.
qe: The 'Prayaga Prashasti' (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), composed in Sanskrit Champu style by court poet Harishena, eulogizes the military conquests of which Gupta emperor?

q: किस चीनी बौद्ध यात्री ने चन्द्रगुप्त द्वितीय के शासनकाल (399–414 ई.) में भारत की यात्रा की और शांत गुप्त समाज का वर्णन 'फो-कुओ-की' में किया?
e:
Fa-Hien (Faxian) visited India during Chandragupta II's reign, noting that people used cowrie shells for small trade and rarely faced harsh punishments (फाह्यान चन्द्रगुप्त द्वितीय के काल में भारत आया था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang, 'Prince of Pilgrims') visited during Harshavardhana's reign (629–645 CE) and wrote 'Si-Yu-Ki'.
2. Aryabhata ('Aryabhatiya', 499 CE) calculated π ≈ 3.1416 and explained solar/lunar eclipses scientifically during the Gupta age.
3. Varahamihira ('Brihat Samhita', 'Panchasiddhantika') and Kalidasa were Navaratnas of Chandragupta II.
qe: Which Chinese Buddhist pilgrim visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II (399–414 CE) and wrote 'Fo-Kuo-Ki' describing the peaceful Gupta society?

q: भारत में सती प्रथा का सर्वप्रथम अभिलेखीय साक्ष्य (510 ई.) किस गुप्तकालीन अभिलेख में मिलता है?
e:
The Eran Pillar Inscription (Sagar district, MP, 510 CE) of Bhanugupta records the immolation of the wife of general Goparaja after he died fighting the Hunas (भानुगुप्त का एरण अभिलेख सती प्रथा का प्रथम अभिलेखीय प्रमाण है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Mandasor inscription (by Vatsabhatti) describes the migration of silk weavers (Tantuvayas) from Lata (Gujarat) to Dashapura.
2. Gupta gold coins were called 'Dinaras' and silver coins 'Rupakas'.
3. Ajanta Cave paintings (Maharashtra) and Dashavatara Temple (Deogarh, UP) represent peak Gupta art.
qe: The earliest epigraphic (inscriptional) evidence of the practice of Sati in India (510 CE) is found in which Gupta-era inscription?

q: सम्राट हर्षवर्धन (606–647 ई.) को नर्मदा नदी के तट पर बादामी के किस चालुक्य शासक ने पराजित किया था, जिसका उल्लेख ऐहोल अभिलेख में मिलता है?
e:
Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II defeated Harsha (~618 CE), stopping Harsha's southward expansion; court poet Ravikirti recorded this in the Aihole Prashasti (ऐहोल अभिलेख के अनुसार पुलकेशिन द्वितीय ने हर्षवर्धन को नर्मदा तट पर हराया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Harsha shifted his capital from Thanesar (Haryana) to Kannauj (UP) and held grand quinquennial assemblies (Maha Moksha Parishad) at Prayaga.
2. Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman I later defeated Pulakeshin II and captured Vatapi (Badami), taking the title 'Vatapikonda'.
3. Harsha authored three Sanskrit dramas: Nagananda, Ratnavali, and Priyadarshika.
qe: Emperor Harshavardhana (606–647 CE) was defeated on the banks of the Narmada river by which Chalukya ruler of Badami, as recorded in the Aihole Inscription?

q: गुप्त प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था में प्रांत को 'भुक्ति' और जिले को 'विषय' कहा जाता था। 'भुक्ति' का प्रमुख अधिकारी कौन होता था?
e:
A Bhukti (province) was governed by an Uparika (or Uparika Maharaja), while a Vishaya (district) was headed by a Vishayapati (भुक्ति का प्रमुख उपरिक कहलाता था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The village was the smallest administrative unit, headed by a Gramika.
2. 'Agrahara' or 'Brahmadeya' referred to tax-free land grants made to Brahmanas and temples.
3. Land tax (Bhaga) was generally 1/6th of the agricultural produce.
qe: In the Gupta administrative system, a province was called 'Bhukti' and a district was called 'Vishaya'. Who headed a 'Bhukti'?

q: किस चोल सम्राट ने लगभग 1010 ई. में तंजावुर में भव्य बृहदीश्वर (राजराजेश्वर) मंदिर का निर्माण कराया था?
e:
Rajaraja I built the granite Dravida-style Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur (a UNESCO Great Living Chola Temple) (राजराज प्रथम ने तंजावुर का बृहदीश्वर मंदिर बनवाया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. His son Rajendra I conquered Sri Lanka, led a naval expedition to Srivijaya (SE Asia), marched to the Ganga, took the title 'Gangaikondachola', and built Gangaikondacholapuram.
2. The Cholas are renowned for local village self-government (Ur and Sabha), vividly detailed in the Uttaramerur Inscription of Parantaka I.
3. Chola bronze sculptures, especially the cosmic 'Nataraja' (dancing Shiva), are world-famous.
qe: Which Chola emperor built the magnificent Brihadeeswarar (Rajarajeshwara) Temple at Thanjavur around 1010 CE?

q: 8वीं से 10वीं शताब्दी ई. के बीच कन्नौज पर नियंत्रण के लिए 'त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष' किन तीन राजवंशों के बीच लड़ा गया था?
e:
The Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj was fought among the Gurjara-Pratiharas (Western/Northern India), Palas (Bengal), and Rashtrakutas (Deccan), with the Pratiharas ultimately securing Kannauj (गुर्जर-प्रतिहार, पाल और राष्ट्रकूट के बीच त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष हुआ)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I built the monolithic rock-cut Kailasa Temple at Ellora (Cave 16).
2. Chandela rulers built the famous Nagara-style temples at Khajuraho (Madhya Pradesh).
3. First Battle of Tarain (1191): Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori; Second Battle of Tarain (1192): Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan.
qe: The 'Tripartite Struggle' (त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष) of the 8th–10th centuries CE for control over the imperial city of Kannauj was fought among which three dynasties?

q: किस राष्ट्रकूट शासक ने कन्नड़ की प्राचीनतम उपलब्ध साहित्यिक कृति 'कविराजमार्ग' की रचना की और जैन विद्वानों को संरक्षण दिया?
e:
Amoghavarsha I (reigned 814–878 CE, capital Manyakheta) wrote 'Kavirajamarga' (Kannada) and 'Prashnottara Ratnamalika' (Sanskrit) (अमोघवर्ष प्रथम ने कविराजमार्ग लिखा)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty (~753 CE) and performed the Hiranyagarbha ritual.
2. Arab traveller Al-Masudi visited India during Indra III's reign; Sulaiman visited during Amoghavarsha's reign.
3. Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala (elected by regional chieftains to end Matsyanyaya in Bengal).
qe: Which Rashtrakuta king authored 'Kavirajamarga', the earliest surviving literary work in Kannada, and patronized Jain scholars?

q: प्रसिद्ध विद्वान अल-बरूनी, जो महमूद गजनवी के साथ भारत आया और जिसने 'किताब-उल-हिन्द' (तहकीक-ए-हिन्द) लिखा, मूलतः किस क्षेत्र का निवासी था?
e:
Abu Rayhan Al-Biruni hailed from Khwarizm (modern Uzbekistan); he learned Sanskrit in India and wrote 'Kitab-ul-Hind' in Arabic covering Indian religion, astronomy, and society (अल-बरूनी ख्वारिज्म का निवासी था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Al-Biruni was the first Muslim scholar to study the Puranas deeply.
2. Firdausi (author of 'Shahnama') and Utbi ('Kitab-ul-Yamini') were also at Mahmud of Ghazni's court.
3. Mahmud of Ghazni invaded India 17 times (1000–1027 CE), most notoriously sacking the Somnath Temple in 1025 CE.
qe: The famous scholar Al-Biruni, who accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni to India and wrote 'Kitab-ul-Hind' (Tahqiq-i-Hind), was originally from which region?

q: दिल्ली सल्तनत का वास्तविक संस्थापक कौन था जिसने इक्ता प्रणाली, चाँदी का 'टका', ताँबे का 'जीतल' और 'तुर्कान-ए-चहलगानी' (चालीसा दल) की शुरुआत की?
e:
Iltutmish (1211–1236) shifted the capital from Lahore to Delhi, completed the Qutub Minar, introduced Tanka & Jital, and institutionalized the Iqta system (इल्तुतमिश दिल्ली सल्तनत का वास्तविक संस्थापक था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Qutb-ud-din Aibak ('Lakh Baksh') founded the Slave/Mamluk dynasty in 1206 and started Qutub Minar (in honour of Sufi saint Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki).
2. Balban crushed the Turkan-i-Chahalgani, adopted the policy of 'Blood and Iron', and introduced 'Sijda' and 'Paibos' (Persian court etiquette) and 'Nauroz'.
3. Razia Sultan (1236–1240) was the only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
qe: Who was the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate who introduced the Iqta system, silver 'Tanka', copper 'Jital', and the 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani' (Corps of Forty)?

q: किस दिल्ली सुल्तान ने बाजार नियंत्रण विभाग 'दीवान-ए-रियासत' की स्थापना की और आवश्यक वस्तुओं के मूल्य निर्धारण हेतु 'शहना-ए-मंडी' की नियुक्ति की?
e:
Alauddin Khalji (1296–1316) implemented strict market reforms in Delhi to maintain a large standing army paid in cash at low salaries (अलाउद्दीन खिलजी ने दीवान-ए-रियासत और शहना-ए-मंडी की स्थापना की)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Alauddin Khalji also introduced 'Diwan-i-Mustakhraj' (arrears recovery), land measurement ('Masahat'), and 'Dag' (horse branding) & 'Chehra' (soldier roll).
2. His general Malik Kafur led successful Deccan expeditions against Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra, and Madurai.
3. Alauddin built Alai Darwaza, Siri Fort, and Hauz Khas in Delhi.
qe: Which Delhi Sultan established the market control department 'Diwan-i-Riyasat' and appointed 'Shahna-i-Mandi' to fix prices of essential commodities?

q: किस दिल्ली सुल्तान ने 'दीवान-ए-खैरात' (दान विभाग), 'दीवान-ए-बंदगान' (दास विभाग), 'दार-उल-शिफा' (निःशुल्क अस्पताल) की स्थापना की और नहरों का विशाल जाल बिछाया?
e:
Firoz Shah Tughlaq (1351–1388) founded cities like Jaunpur, Firozabad, Hisar, and Fatehabad, brought two Ashokan pillars (Topra & Meerut) to Delhi, and imposed Jizya separately on Brahmanas (फिरोज शाह तुगलक ने ये कल्याणकारी विभाग और नहरें बनवाईं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq was the first Sultan to start canal irrigation, though Firoz Shah expanded it massively.
2. Firoz Shah Tughlaq wrote his autobiography 'Futuhat-i-Firozshahi'.
3. He levied four Quranic taxes: Kharaj, Khams, Zakat, and Jizya, plus an irrigation tax 'Haqq-i-Sharb'.
qe: Which Sultan of Delhi set up 'Diwan-i-Khairat' (charity department), 'Diwan-i-Bandagan' (department of slaves), 'Dar-ul-Shifa' (free hospital), and built a vast network of canals?

q:
सूची-I (दिल्ली सल्तनत विभाग) को सूची-II (कार्य) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. दीवान-ए-विजारत
2. दीवान-ए-अर्ज
3. दीवान-ए-इंशा
4. दीवान-ए-रिसालत
सूची-II:
(a) धार्मिक/विदेश मामले
(b) शाही पत्राचार
(c) सैन्य विभाग
(d) वित्त एवं राजस्व
e:
Diwan-i-Wizarat = Finance/Wazir; Diwan-i-Ariz = Military (set up by Balban); Diwan-i-Insha = Royal correspondence; Diwan-i-Risalat = Religious/diplomatic affairs (1-d, 2-c, 3-b, 4-a)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi (agriculture) was created by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
2. Diwan-i-Qaza was headed by the Qazi-ul-Quzat (Chief Justice).
3. Barid-i-Mamalik was the head of the intelligence and postal network.
qe:
Match List-I (Delhi Sultanate Department) with List-II (Function) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Diwan-i-Wizarat
2. Diwan-i-Ariz
3. Diwan-i-Insha
4. Diwan-i-Risalat
List-II:
(a) Religious affairs / Foreign correspondence
(b) Royal correspondence
(c) Military department
(d) Finance & Revenue

q: पानीपत का प्रथम युद्ध (21 अप्रैल 1526), जिसने दिल्ली सल्तनत का अंत कर मुगल साम्राज्य की नींव रखी, बाबर और किस लोदी शासक के बीच लड़ा गया था?
e:
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi using the Tulughma flanking tactic and Ottoman-style artillery (Rumi method) at the First Battle of Panipat (1526); Ibrahim Lodi was the only Delhi Sultan killed on the battlefield (बाबर ने इब्राहिम लोदी को पराजित किया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Babur's four major Indian battles: Panipat (1526, Ibrahim Lodi), Khanwa (1527, Rana Sanga), Chanderi (1528, Medini Rai), and Ghaghra (1529, Afghans).
2. Babur wrote his autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Baburi' (Baburnama) in Chagatai Turki.
3. Sikandar Lodi introduced the 'Gaj-i-Sikandari' land measurement unit (32 digits).
qe: The First Battle of Panipat (21 April 1526), which ended the Delhi Sultanate and established the Mughal Empire, was fought between Babur and which Lodi ruler?

q: संत विद्यारण्य के आशीर्वाद से 1336 ई. में तुंगभद्रा नदी के तट पर विजयनगर साम्राज्य की स्थापना किसने की थी?
e:
Brothers Harihara I and Bukka I of the Sangama dynasty founded the Vijayanagara Empire (capital Hampi) in 1336 CE (हरिहर और बुक्का ने 1336 में विजयनगर की स्थापना की)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Four dynasties ruled Vijayanagara in order: Sangama → Saluva → Tuluva → Aravidu.
2. Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva dynasty, 1509–1529) authored 'Amuktamalyada' (Telugu) and 'Jambavati Kalyanam' (Sanskrit), and patronized the 'Ashtadiggajas' (8 Telugu poets including Tenali Rama).
3. The Battle of Talikota / Rakshasi-Tangadi (1565) shattered Vijayanagara power.
qe: Who founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE on the banks of the Tungabhadra river with the blessings of Sage Vidyaranya?

q: किस सूफी संत की दरगाह अजमेर (राजस्थान) में स्थित है, और जो भारत में चिश्ती सिलसिले के संस्थापक थे?
e:
Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti ('Gharib Nawaz') arrived in India around 1192 CE and settled at Ajmer, founding the Chishti order in India (ख्वाजा मुईनुद्दीन चिश्ती भारत में चिश्ती सिलसिले के संस्थापक थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya ('Mahbub-i-Ilahi', Delhi) famously remarked 'Hunuz Dilli Dur Ast' (दिल्ली अभी दूर है) to Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq.
2. Sheikh Salim Chishti's white marble dargah is at Fatehpur Sikri (Akbar revered him).
3. Suhrawardi order was established in India by Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya (Multan); Naqshbandi order by Khwaja Baqi Billah (and Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi).
qe: Which Sufi saint's dargah is located at Ajmer (Rajasthan), and who was the founder of the Chishti Silsila in India?

q: फारस (शाहरुख का राजदूत) के किस विदेशी यात्री ने देवराय द्वितीय के शासनकाल (1443 ई.) में विजयनगर की यात्रा की और इसकी सात संकेंद्रित किलेबंदी की प्रशंसा की?
e:
Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq visited Deva Raya II's court in 1443 CE (अब्दुर रज्जाक देवराय द्वितीय के काल में विजयनगर आया था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Niccolo de Conti (Italy) visited under Deva Raya I (~1420); Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa (Portugal) visited under Krishnadevaraya.
2. Fernao Nuniz (Portugal) visited under Achyuta Deva Raya.
3. The Bahmani Kingdom was founded by Alauddin Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu) in 1347 CE (capital Gulbarga, later Bidar).
qe: Which foreign traveller from Persia (ambassador of Shah Rukh) visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Deva Raya II (1443 CE) and praised its seven concentric fortifications?

q: 'नायंकर' (सैन्य प्रमुख भू-अनुदान) और 'आयगर' (12 वंशानुगत ग्राम अधिकारी) प्रणालियाँ किस दक्षिण भारतीय साम्राज्य की प्रमुख प्रशासनिक विशेषताएँ थीं?
e:
Amara-Nayakas (military commanders given territories called Amaram) and the 12-member Ayagar village council characterized Vijayanagara administration (नायंकर व आयगर प्रणालियाँ विजयनगर साम्राज्य की विशेषताएँ थीं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Vittalaswami Temple (famous for its stone chariot and musical pillars) and Virupaksha Temple are architectural gems of Hampi.
2. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on the banks of the Tungabhadra river in Karnataka.
3. Mahmud Gawan was the celebrated Prime Minister (Wazir) of the Bahmani Kingdom who built the Bidar Madrasa.
qe: The 'Nayankara' (military chief land-grant) and 'Ayagar' (12 hereditary village functionaries) systems were hallmark administrative features of which South Indian empire?

q: मुगल साम्राज्य में 'मनसबदारी' प्रथा (जात और सवार पदों के साथ) तथा 'दहसाला' (टोडरमल बंदोबस्त) भू-राजस्व प्रणाली की शुरुआत किसने की?
e:
Emperor Akbar introduced the Mansabdari system (inspired by Mongol decimal ranking) and Raja Todar Mal's Zabti/Dahsala revenue system (1580) (अकबर ने मनसबदारी और दहसाला व्यवस्था शुरू की)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Akbar abolished Pilgrimage Tax (1563) and Jizya (1564), built Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri (1575), issued Mahzar (1579), and propounded Din-i-Ilahi (1582).
2. Abul Fazl authored 'Akbarnama' and 'Ain-i-Akbari'.
3. Jahangir introduced the 'Du-aspa Sih-aspa' rank; Shah Jahan introduced the 'Month-scale' system in Mansabdari.
qe: Who introduced the 'Mansabdari' system (with dual ranks Zat and Sawar) and the 'Dahsala' (Todar Mal Bandobast) land revenue system in the Mughal Empire?

q: शेरशाह सूरी (1540–1545), जिसने हुमायूँ को चौसा (1539) और कन्नौज (1540) में हराया, ने कौन-सा मानक चाँदी का सिक्का चलाया जो आधुनिक भारतीय रुपये का पूर्वज बना?
e:
Sher Shah Suri issued the 178-grain pure silver 'Rupiya' and copper 'Dam', built the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-i-Azam from Sonargaon to Peshawar), and introduced Patta and Qabuliyat (शेरशाह सूरी ने चाँदी का 'रुपया' और ताँबे का 'दाम' चलाया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Sher Shah's octagonal tomb stands amidst a lake at Sasaram (Bihar).
2. He died in 1545 during the siege of Kalinjar Fort (Banda, UP) from a gunpowder explosion.
3. His revenue system served as the blueprint for Akbar's Todar Mal reforms.
qe: Sher Shah Suri (1540–1545), who defeated Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj/Bilgram (1540), introduced which standardized silver coin that became the precursor of the modern Indian Rupee?

q: छत्रपति शिवाजी महाराज के 'अष्टप्रधान' (आठ मंत्रियों की परिषद) में विदेश मामलों का प्रभारी मंत्री कौन होता था?
e:
Sumant (or Dabir) handled Foreign Affairs in Shivaji's Ashtapradhan (सुमन्त विदेश मंत्री था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Peshwa = Prime Minister; Amatya/Majumdar = Finance; Waqia-Navis = Intelligence/Home; Sachiv/Surunavis = Royal correspondence; Sar-i-Naubat = Commander-in-Chief; Panditrao = Religion; Nyayadhish = Chief Justice.
2. Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad Fort in June 1674 by Pandit Gaga Bhatt of Varanasi.
3. Chauth (1/4th of revenue from neighbouring territories to avoid raids) and Sardeshmukhi (1/10th hereditary levy) were key Maratha taxes.
qe: In Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's 'Ashtapradhan' (Council of Eight Ministers), who was the minister in charge of Foreign Affairs?

q: पुरन्दर की संधि (जून 1665) छत्रपति शिवाजी और सम्राट औरंगजेब का प्रतिनिधित्व करने वाले किस मुगल सेनापति के बीच हस्ताक्षरित हुई थी?
e:
Under the Treaty of Purandar (1665) with Mirza Raja Jai Singh of Amber, Shivaji ceded 23 of his 35 forts to the Mughals and agreed to visit Agra (पुरन्दर की संधि शिवाजी और मिर्जा राजा जयसिंह के बीच हुई)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Earlier, Shivaji had killed Bijapur general Afzal Khan (1659) and launched a daring night raid on Shaista Khan in Pune (1663).
2. Mughal painting reached its zenith under Jahangir (Ustad Mansur, Abul Hasan, Bishandas).
3. Mughal architecture reached its peak under Shah Jahan (Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Jama Masjid).
qe: The Treaty of Purandar (June 1665) was signed between Chhatrapati Shivaji and which Mughal commander representing Emperor Aurangzeb?

q: किस मुगल शहजादे ने 52 उपनिषदों का फारसी में 'सिर्र-ए-अकबर' नाम से अनुवाद किया और 'मज्म-उल-बहरैन' (दो महासागरों का संगम) की रचना की?
e:
Dara Shikoh (eldest son of Shah Jahan, follower of the Qadiri Sufi order) translated the Upanishads as 'Sirr-i-Akbar' and wrote 'Majma-ul-Bahrain' to bridge Hindu and Islamic mysticism (दारा शिकोह ने सिर्र-ए-अकबर व मज्म-उल-बहरैन की रचना की)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Lane-Poole called Dara Shikoh 'Little Akbar' (लघु अकबर).
2. In the War of Succession (1658–59), Aurangzeb defeated Dara Shikoh at the Battles of Samugarh (1658) and Deorai (1659).
3. Aurangzeb re-imposed Jizya in 1679 and annexed Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687).
qe: Which Mughal prince translated 52 Upanishads into Persian under the title 'Sirr-i-Akbar' (The Great Secret) and authored 'Majma-ul-Bahrain' (Mingling of the Two Oceans)?

q: 1793 में बंगाल, बिहार और उड़ीसा में 'स्थायी बंदोबस्त' (जमींदारी प्रथा) किसने लागू की थी?
e:
Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in 1793 (planned with Sir John Shore), fixing land revenue permanently with Zamindars (लॉर्ड कॉर्नवालिस ने 1793 में स्थायी बंदोबस्त लागू किया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Ryotwari System (Madras & Bombay, 1820) was introduced by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read.
2. Mahalwari System (North-Western Provinces/UP, Punjab, Central India, 1822) was devised by Holt Mackenzie and revised by Robert Merttins Bird.
3. Lord Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance (1798, first accepted by Nizam of Hyderabad); Lord Dalhousie used the Doctrine of Lapse (first annexed Satara in 1848).
qe: Who introduced the 'Permanent Settlement' (स्थायी बंदोबस्त / Zamindari system) in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa in 1793?

q: 1856 में लॉर्ड डलहौजी ने किस भारतीय राज्य का विलय व्यपगत सिद्धांत (Doctrine of Lapse) के तहत नहीं, बल्कि 'कुशासन' (maladministration) के आरोप में किया था?
e:
Awadh (ruled by Nawab Wajid Ali Shah) was annexed in February 1856 based on James Outram's report alleging misgovernance, deeply alienating Bengal Army sepoys from Awadh and fuelling the 1857 Revolt (अवध का विलय कुशासन के आरोप में किया गया था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. States annexed via Doctrine of Lapse: Satara (1848), Jaitpur & Sambalpur (1849), Baghat (1850), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), Nagpur (1854).
2. Dalhousie also started India's first passenger railway (Bombay to Thane, 16 April 1853), telegraph line (Calcutta–Agra), and modern postal system.
3. The Queen's Proclamation of 1 November 1858 (read by Lord Canning at Allahabad) abolished the Doctrine of Lapse.
qe: Which Indian state was annexed by Lord Dalhousie in 1856 NOT under the Doctrine of Lapse, but on the pretext of 'maladministration' (कुशासन)?

q:
सूची-I (यूरोपीय व्यापारिक कंपनी) को सूची-II (भारत में प्रथम कारखाना) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. पुर्तगाली
2. डच
3. अंग्रेज
4. फ्रांसीसी
सूची-II:
(a) सूरत (1668)
(b) मसूलीपट्टनम (1605)
(c) कोचीन (1503)
(d) सूरत / मसूलीपट्टनम (1611–13)
e:

q: संविधान सभा और अंतरिम सरकार की रूपरेखा तैयार करने के लिए पैथिक-लॉरेंस, स्टैफोर्ड क्रिप्स और ए. वी. अलेक्जेंडर के साथ मार्च 1946 में कौन-सा ब्रिटिश मिशन भारत आया था?

q: एकल महामहाद्वीप 'पैंजिया' और महासागर 'पैंथालासा' की अवधारणा वाला 'महाद्वीपीय विस्थापन सिद्धांत' 1912 में किसके द्वारा प्रस्तुत किया गया था?

German meteorologist Alfred Wegener proposed Continental Drift Theory in 1912 ('The Origin of Continents and Oceans', 1915) (अल्फ्रेड वेगनर ने महाद्वीपीय विस्थापन सिद्धांत दिया)।

q: पृथ्वी के वायुमंडल की किस परत में ओजोन परत स्थित है जो हानिकारक पराबैंगनी (UV) सौर विकिरण को अवशोषित करती है?
e:
The Stratosphere (~15–50 km altitude) houses the ozone layer (peaking at ~20–35 km) and has calm, cloud-free conditions ideal for jet aircraft (ओजोन परत समतापमंडल में स्थित है)।

qe: Which layer of the Earth's atmosphere contains the Ozone layer that absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) solar radiation?

The Humboldt (Peru) Current is a cold Pacific current flowing northward along Chile and Peru, suppressing convection and causing the Atacama Desert; its periodic weakening causes El Niño (हम्बोल्ट/पेरू धारा ठंडी धारा है)।

q: पिघले हुए मैग्मा या लावा के ठंडा होकर जमने से किस प्रकार की चट्टान (जैसे ग्रेनाइट और बेसाल्ट) का निर्माण होता है?
e:
Igneous rocks ('Primary rocks', non-stratified, devoid of fossils) form from magma (intrusive: Granite) or lava (extrusive: Basalt) (आग्नेय चट्टानें मैग्मा/लावा के ठंडा होने से बनती हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:

2. Metamorphic transformations: Limestone → Marble; Sandstone → Quartzite; Shale → Slate; Granite → Gneiss; Coal → Graphite/Diamond.
3. About 75% of Earth's land surface is covered by sedimentary rocks, though igneous/metamorphic rocks dominate Earth's crust by volume.
qe: Which type of rock is formed by the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava (such as Granite and Basalt)?

q: कोपेन के जलवायु वर्गीकरण में जलवायु कूट 'Cs' किसे निरूपित करता है?
e:
In Köppen's scheme, 'C' stands for warm temperate (mesothermal) and lowercase 's' stands for dry summer—representing the classic Mediterranean climate (olive, grape, citrus cultivation) (कोपेन का 'Cs' भूमध्यसागरीय जलवायु को दर्शाता है)।

2. Mediterranean climate occurs on western margins of continents between 30°–45° N and S due to seasonal shifting of pressure belts.
3. Winter rainfall in Mediterranean regions comes from onshore Westerlies.
qe: In Köppen's Climatic Classification, what does the climatic code 'Cs' represent?
oe: Mediterranean climate with dry summers and wet winters

q: वृहद ज्वार (Spring Tides), जिनमें ज्वारीय परिसर सर्वाधिक होता है, चंद्रमा की किन कलाओं के दौरान आते हैं?
e:
Spring tides occur at Syzygy (New Moon and Full Moon) when Sun, Earth, and Moon align in a straight line and their gravitational pulls combine (अमावस्या और पूर्णिमा को वृहद ज्वार आते हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Neap tides (लघु ज्वार) occur at First and Third Quarters (Quadrature) when Sun and Moon are at 90° relative to Earth.
2. The Bay of Fundy (Canada) experiences the world's highest tidal range (~15–16 m); in India, the Gulf of Khambhat / Okha (Gujarat) sees the highest tides.
3. Normal interval between two successive high tides is 12 hours 26 minutes (two high tides per 24 hours 52 minutes).
qe: Spring Tides (वृहद ज्वार), which exhibit the highest tidal range, occur during which lunar phases?

q: प्रमुख खुले महासागरों में किस महासागर की औसत लवणता सर्वाधिक है, तथा झीलों में विश्व की सर्वाधिक लवणता वाली झील कौन-सी है?
o: Atlantic Ocean; Lake Van (Turkey) / Don Juan Pond
e:
Among open oceans, the Atlantic Ocean has the highest average salinity (~35.6‰, peaking ~37‰ in the Sargasso Sea), while Lake Van (Turkey, ~330‰) and Dead Sea (~238–340‰) / Don Juan Pond are the world's saltiest water bodies (अटलांटिक महासागर की लवणता सर्वाधिक है और तुर्की की वान झील सर्वाधिक लवणीय झीलों में है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Average salinity of ocean water is 35 parts per thousand (35‰); Sodium Chloride (NaCl) accounts for ~77.8% of dissolved salts.
2. Highest salinity occurs near the Tropics (20°–30° N/S) where evaporation exceeds precipitation—not at the Equator (heavy rainfall dilutes salinity).
3. Isohalines are lines connecting places of equal ocean salinity.
qe: Which ocean has the highest average salinity among the major open oceans, and which enclosed water body has the highest salinity in the world among lakes?
oe: Atlantic Ocean; Lake Van (Turkey) / Don Juan Pond

q: भूकंप की तीव्रता/परिमाण मापने के लिए किस यंत्र का उपयोग किया जाता है, और कौन-सा पैमाना भूकंप के परिमाण को लघुगणकीय रूप से मापता है?
e:
A Seismograph records seismic waves (P, S, L waves), and the Richter Scale (and modern Moment Magnitude Scale) measures magnitude, whereas the Mercalli Scale measures visible damage intensity (सीस्मोग्राफ व रिक्टर पैमाना)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Primary (P) waves are longitudinal and travel through solids, liquids, and gases; Secondary (S) waves are transverse and CANNOT pass through the liquid outer core (creating the S-wave shadow zone beyond 103°).
2. Surface (L / Love & Rayleigh) waves are the slowest and most destructive.
3. The Circum-Pacific Belt ('Ring of Fire') accounts for ~68% of world earthquakes and most active volcanoes.
qe: Which instrument is used to measure the intensity/magnitude of earthquakes, and which scale measures earthquake energy magnitude logarithmically?

q: पृथ्वी के घूर्णन के कारण उत्पन्न 'कोरिओलिस बल' गतिमान पवनों और महासागरीय धाराओं को किन दिशाओं में विक्षेपित करता है?
o: Left in Northern Hemisphere, Right in Southern Hemisphere
Right in Northern Hemisphere, Left in Southern Hemisphere
Always toward the Equator in both hemispheres
Always toward the Poles in both hemispheres
e:
According to Ferrel's Law, the Coriolis force deflects moving bodies to the RIGHT in the Northern Hemisphere and to the LEFT in the Southern Hemisphere (उत्तरी गोलार्ध में दाईं ओर और दक्षिणी गोलार्ध में बाईं ओर)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Coriolis force is ZERO at the Equator (which is why tropical cyclones do not form right at the Equator) and MAXIMUM at the Poles.
2. Geostrophic winds blow parallel to isobars in the upper atmosphere when Pressure Gradient Force balances Coriolis Force.
3. Tropical cyclones rotate counter-clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.
qe: The 'Coriolis Force', caused by the rotation of the Earth, deflects moving winds and ocean currents in which directions?
oe: Left in Northern Hemisphere, Right in Southern Hemisphere
Right in Northern Hemisphere, Left in Southern Hemisphere
Always toward the Equator in both hemispheres
Always toward the Poles in both hemispheres

q: 'समस्थिति' (Isostasy) की अवधारणा के दो प्रसिद्ध मॉडल— 'समान घनत्व व भिन्न गहराई (पर्वतों की जड़ें)' तथा 'भिन्न घनत्व व समान क्षतिपूर्ति तल'— क्रमशः किसके द्वारा प्रस्तुत किए गए?
o: George Airy and John Henry Pratt
John Henry Pratt and George Airy
e:
Sir George Airy (1855) proposed 'uniform density, varying thickness' (like icebergs floating in water—higher mountains have deeper roots), while Archdeacon John Henry Pratt (1859) proposed 'varying density, uniform depth of compensation' (एरी व प्राट के सिद्धांत)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The term 'Isostasy' was coined by American geologist Clarence Dutton in 1889.
2. J. F. Hayford and William Bowie later refined Pratt's model mathematically.
3. W. A. Heiskanen combined both Airy and Pratt concepts in 1933.
qe: The concept of 'Isostasy' (समस्थिति), explaining the gravitational equilibrium of Earth's crustal blocks, saw two famous models—'Uniform Density with Varying Thickness (Roots of Mountains)' and 'Varying Density with Uniform Depth of Compensation'—proposed respectively by:
oe: George Airy and John Henry Pratt
John Henry Pratt and George Airy

q: कौन-सा बायोम स्थायी तुषारभूमि (permafrost), अत्यंत छोटे ग्रीष्मकाल और काई, लाइकेन व बौनी झाड़ियों वाली वनस्पति के लिए जाना जाता है?
e:
The Arctic/Alpine Tundra biome (treeless plains north of the Arctic Circle) features permanently frozen subsoil (permafrost), mosses, and lichens (टुंड्रा बायोम में पर्माफ्रॉस्ट, काई और लाइकेन पाए जाते हैं)।

2. Temperate grasslands by region: Prairies (N. America), Pampas (Argentina), Steppes (Eurasia), Veld (S. Africa), Downs (Australia), Canterbury (New Zealand).
3. Tropical grasslands: Savanna (Africa), Llanos (Venezuela), Campos (Brazil).
qe: Which biome is characterized by permafrost, extremely short summers, and vegetation dominated by mosses, lichens, and dwarf shrubs?

q: किसे 'आधुनिक मानव भूगोल का जनक' माना जाता है और जिन्होंने प्रसिद्ध ग्रन्थ 'एंथ्रोपोजियोग्राफी' (Anthropogeographie) की रचना की?
e:
German geographer Friedrich Ratzel ('Anthropogeographie', 1882; 'Lebensraum') is regarded as the Father of Human Geography and a key exponent of Environmental Determinism (फ्रेडरिक रेटजेल मानव भूगोल के जनक हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Paul Vidal de la Blache (France) founded 'Possibilism' (संभववाद — term coined by Lucien Febvre).
2. Griffith Taylor (Australia) proposed 'Neo-Determinism' or 'Stop-and-Go Determinism' (नव-निश्चयवाद / रुको और जाओ निश्चयवाद).
3. Ellen Churchill Semple (USA, student of Ratzel) wrote 'Influences of Geographic Environment' (1911).
qe: Who is universally recognized as the 'Father of Modern Human Geography' and authored the landmark work 'Anthropogeographie'?

q:
सूची-I (प्रमुख विश्व जनजाति) को सूची-II (पारंपरिक आवास) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. बुशमैन (सैन)
2. पिग्मी
3. मसाई
4. एस्किमो (इन्यूट)
सूची-II:
(a) आर्कटिक टुंड्रा (ग्रीनलैंड/कनाडा)
(b) पूर्वी अफ्रीकी उच्चभूमि (केन्या/तंजानिया)

(d) कालाहारी मरुस्थल (दक्षिणी अफ्रीका)
e:
Bushmen inhabit Kalahari Desert; Pygmies inhabit Congo rainforest; Masai are pastoralists of Kenya/Tanzania (Kraal huts); Eskimos inhabit Arctic Tundra (Igloos, Kayaks, Harpoons) (1-d, 2-c, 3-b, 4-a)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Khirgiz (Central Asia) live in 'Yurts'; Bedouins inhabit Arabian Desert; Sakai & Semang inhabit Malaysia; Ainu inhabit Japan; Maori inhabit New Zealand.
2. Eskimos belong to the Mongoloid racial stock; Pygmies and Bushmen belong to Negroid/Capoid groups.
3. Red Indians (Native Americans) are indigenous to North/South America.
qe:
Match List-I (Major World Tribe) with List-II (Traditional Habitat) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Bushmen (San)
2. Pygmies
3. Masai
4. Eskimo (Inuit)
List-II:
(a) Arctic Tundra (Greenland/Canada)
(b) East African Highlands (Kenya/Tanzania)
(c) Congo Basin (Central Africa)
(d) Kalahari Desert (Southern Africa)

q: जनसांख्यिकीय संक्रमण मॉडल (वॉरेन थॉम्पसन व फ्रैंक नोटेस्टीन) में द्वितीय अवस्था (प्रारंभिक विस्तार अवस्था) की प्रमुख विशेषता क्या है?
o: High birth rate and high death rate (slow growth)
High birth rate and rapidly declining death rate (population explosion)
Low birth rate and low death rate (stationary population)
Birth rate falling below death rate (negative growth)
e:
Stage II sees a sharp drop in mortality due to improved healthcare/sanitation while fertility remains high, producing rapid population growth ('Population Explosion') (द्वितीय अवस्था में उच्च जन्म दर और तेजी से गिरती मृत्यु दर के कारण जनसंख्या विस्फोट होता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Stage I: High stationary (both BR & DR high); Stage III: Late expanding (BR falls, DR low — India is currently in late Stage III).
2. Stage IV: Low stationary (both BR & DR low — USA, Europe); Stage V: Declining population (Japan, Germany).
3. Thomas Malthus ('An Essay on the Principle of Population', 1798) argued population grows geometrically (1, 2, 4, 8) while food grows arithmetically (1, 2, 3, 4).
qe: In the Demographic Transition Model (proposed by Warren Thompson & Frank Notestein), Stage II (Early Expanding Stage) is characterized by:
oe: High birth rate and high death rate (slow growth)
High birth rate and rapidly declining death rate (population explosion)
Low birth rate and low death rate (stationary population)
Birth rate falling below death rate (negative growth)

q: नगरीय बस्तियों के आकार, संख्या और षट्कोणीय स्थानिक वितरण की व्याख्या करने के लिए 'केंद्रीय स्थल सिद्धांत' (1933) किसने प्रस्तुत किया?
e:
German geographer Walter Christaller formulated Central Place Theory in 1933 based on southern Germany, using hexagonal market areas and K = 3 (marketing), K = 4 (transport), and K = 7 (administrative) principles (वाल्टर क्रिस्टालर ने केंद्रीय स्थल सिद्धांत दिया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Urban land-use models: Concentric Zone Model — E. W. Burgess (1925); Sector Model — Homer Hoyt (1939); Multiple Nuclei Model — Harris & Ullman (1945).
2. Patrick Geddes coined the term 'Conurbation' (सन्नगर, 1915); Jean Gottmann coined 'Megalopolis' (1957).
3. Mark Jefferson proposed the 'Law of Primate City' (1939); G. K. Zipf formulated the 'Rank-Size Rule' (1949).
qe: Who proposed the 'Central Place Theory' (केंद्रीय स्थल सिद्धांत, 1933) to explain the size, number, and hexagonal spatial distribution of urban settlements?

q: नदियों के किनारों, नहरों, सड़कों या रेलमार्गों के सहारे सामान्यतः किस प्रकार का ग्रामीण बस्ती प्रतिरूप विकसित होता है?
e:
Linear (ribbon) settlements stretch along transport arteries (roads, railways) or water channels (rivers, canals, coastlines) (नदी, नहर व सड़क के किनारे रेखीय प्रतिरूप विकसित होता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Circular patterns develop around lakes, ponds, or oases.
2. Rectangular/checkerboard patterns occur in fertile flat plains (e.g., Ganga-Sutlej plain) where roads intersect at right angles.
3. Star-like patterns emerge where several roads converge at a central junction.
qe: Which rural settlement pattern typically develops along riverbanks, canals, roads, or railway lines?

q: एवरेट ली के 'प्रवास के प्रतिकर्ष-आकर्ष सिद्धांत' (1966) के अनुसार, गंतव्य नगरों की ओर प्रवासियों को आकर्षित करने वाला 'आकर्षण कारक' (Pull Factor) कौन-सा है?
o: Drought and crop failure in villages
Better employment, higher wages, and quality education/healthcare
Political instability and civil conflict at origin
e:
Pull factors draw people toward a destination (better jobs, wages, education, healthcare, safety), while Push factors compel people to leave their origin (drought, poverty, unemployment, conflict) (बेहतर रोजगार, उच्च वेतन और शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य आकर्षण कारक हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. E. G. Ravenstein formulated the earliest 'Laws of Migration' (1885), noting most migrants move short distances (step-migration).
2. In India, rural-to-urban migration is dominated by males (economic/employment), while rural-to-rural migration is dominated by females (marriage).
3. Brain Drain refers to the emigration of highly skilled professionals from developing to developed countries.
qe: According to Everett Lee's 'Push–Pull Theory of Migration' (1966), which of the following is a 'Pull Factor' (आकर्षण कारक) attracting migrants to destination cities?
oe: Drought and crop failure in villages
Better employment, higher wages, and quality education/healthcare
Political instability and civil conflict at origin

q: राजनीतिक भूगोल में 'हार्टलैंड सिद्धांत' (हृदय स्थल सिद्धांत — 1904) किसके द्वारा प्रतिपादित किया गया था?
e:
British geographer Sir Halford Mackinder presented the 'Geographical Pivot of History' (1904) and 'Heartland Theory' (1919) (हैल्फोर्ड मैकिंडर ने हार्टलैंड सिद्धांत दिया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Nicholas Spykman countered Mackinder with the 'Rimland Theory' (1944).
2. A. T. Mahan propounded the 'Sea Power Theory'; Rudolf Kjellen coined the term 'Geopolitics' (1899).
3. Friedrich Ratzel proposed the 'Organic Theory of the State'.
qe: The term 'Heartland Theory' ("Who rules East Europe commands the Heartland; who rules the Heartland commands the World-Island") in Political Geography was propounded in 1904 by:

q: निम्नलिखित में से किस महाद्वीप की कुल जनसंख्या का सर्वाधिक प्रतिशत नगरीय क्षेत्रों में निवास करता है (सर्वाधिक नगरीकरण स्तर)?
e:
North America (~82–83%) and South America/Latin America (~81%) have the highest urbanization rates among inhabited continents, followed by Europe (~75%), Asia (~52%), and Africa (~44%) (उत्तरी अमेरिका में नगरीकरण प्रतिशत सर्वाधिक है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Asia houses ~60% of the world's total population, while Africa has the fastest population growth rate.
2. Tokyo (Japan) is the world's most populous metropolitan agglomeration, followed by Delhi and Shanghai.
3. World Population Day is observed on 11 July every year.
qe: Which of the following continents has the highest percentage of its total population living in urban areas (highest urbanization level)?

q: जोहान हेनरिक वॉन थ्यूनेन के 'कृषि अवस्थिति सिद्धांत' (1826, 'द आइसोलेटेड स्टेट') में केंद्रीय बाजार नगर के सबसे निकटतम वलय (जोन 1) में कौन-सी कृषि गतिविधि स्थित होती है?
e:
Because milk, vegetables, and fruits are highly perishable with high transport costs, Market Gardening & Dairying occupy Zone 1; Zone 2 is Forestry/Firewood, Zones 3–5 are Grain/Crop farming, and Zone 6 is Livestock Ranching (जोन 1 में बाजार बागवानी व डेयरी उद्योग होते हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Von Thünen's model is driven by 'Locational Rent' (Economic Rent) = Yield × (Market Price - Production Cost) - (Yield × Transport Rate × Distance).
2. Alfred Weber (1909) proposed the 'Least Cost Theory of Industrial Location' using Material Index (MI = Weight of localized raw materials ÷ Weight of finished product).
3. If MI > 1 (weight-losing industry like iron & steel, sugar), industry locates near raw materials; if MI < 1 (weight-gaining like soft drinks), near the market.
qe: In Johann Heinrich von Thünen's 'Agricultural Location Theory' (1826, 'The Isolated State'), which agricultural activity occupies the innermost ring (Zone 1) closest to the central market city?

q: 'स्थानांतरी कृषि' को विश्व भर में विभिन्न क्षेत्रीय नामों से जाना जाता है। इसे क्रमशः पूर्वोत्तर भारत और इंडोनेशिया/मलेशिया में क्या कहा जाता है?
e:
Shifting cultivation is called 'Jhum' in Northeast India and 'Ladang' in Indonesia/Malaysia (पूर्वोत्तर भारत में झूम और इंडोनेशिया/मलेशिया में लदांग)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Other world names: Milpa (Mexico/Central America), Roca (Brazil), Ray (Vietnam), Chena (Sri Lanka), Caingin (Philippines), Fang (Equatorial Africa).
2. Other Indian regional names: Podu (Andhra/Telangana), Bewar/Dahiya (MP), Kumari (Western Ghats), Valre/Waltre (SE Rajasthan).
3. Shifting cultivation is a primitive subsistence slash-and-burn practice that causes deforestation if fallow periods shorten.
qe: 'Shifting Cultivation' (स्थानांतरी कृषि) is known by different regional names worldwide. What is it called in Northeast India and in Indonesia/Malaysia respectively?

q: राइन नदी बेसिन में समृद्ध बिटुमिनस कोयला भंडार के साथ स्थित जर्मनी का कौन-सा औद्योगिक क्षेत्र 'यूरोप का औद्योगिक हृदय' कहलाता है?
e:
The Ruhr Valley (Germany) is Europe's premier coal and heavy iron-steel industrial region; in India, the Damodar Valley / Chota Nagpur Plateau is called the 'Ruhr of India' (रूर घाटी को यूरोप का औद्योगिक हृदय कहा जाता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Detroit (USA) is famous for automobiles; Pittsburgh (USA) is the 'Iron and Steel Capital'; Silicon Valley (California) for IT.
2. Osaka (Japan) is called the 'Manchester of Japan'; Nagoya is the 'Detroit of Japan'.
3. Kimberley (South Africa) is world-famous for diamonds; Witwatersrand (Johannesburg) for gold; Mesabi Range (USA) for iron ore.
qe: Which industrial region of Germany, located in the Rhine river basin with rich bituminous coal reserves, is famously called the 'Industrial Heart of Europe'?

q: विश्व में प्राकृतिक रबर का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक देश कौन-सा है, तथा कॉफी (कहवा) का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक देश कौन-सा है?
e:
Thailand leads global natural rubber production (followed by Indonesia and Vietnam), and Brazil leads global coffee production (where large coffee plantations are called 'Fazendas' and Santos is the 'Coffee Port') (थाईलैंड प्राकृतिक रबर व ब्राजील कॉफी उत्पादन में प्रथम हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. In India, Kerala leads in Natural Rubber (>70%) and Karnataka leads in Coffee (>70%, Bababudan Hills).
2. China leads globally in Rice, Wheat, Tea, Cotton, Coal, and Gold production.
3. Chile is the world's largest producer of Copper (Chuquicamata mine).
qe: Which country is the world's largest producer of Natural Rubber, and which country is the largest producer of Coffee?

q: कौन-सी अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समुद्री नहर भूमध्य सागर को लाल सागर से जोड़ती है, जिससे यूरोप और भारत के बीच समुद्री मार्ग अत्यंत छोटा हो गया?
e:
The Suez Canal (Egypt, opened in 1869, ~193 km long, linking Port Said on the Mediterranean to Port Suez on the Red Sea) cut the London–Mumbai sea voyage by ~7,000 km (स्वेज नहर भूमध्य सागर को लाल सागर से जोड़ती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Panama Canal (opened 1914) connects the Atlantic Ocean and Pacific Ocean using a lock system (Gatun Lake).
2. Kiel Canal (Germany) connects the North Sea and Baltic Sea; Soo Canal connects Lake Superior and Lake Huron.
3. The North Atlantic Sea Route ('Big Trunk Route') between Western Europe and Eastern North America is the busiest ocean trade route in the world.
qe: Which international maritime canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea, drastically shortening the sea route between Europe and India?

q:
सूची-I (आर्थिक क्रिया क्षेत्र) को सूची-II (उदाहरण) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. प्राथमिक (रेड-कॉलर)
2. द्वितीयक (ब्लू-कॉलर)
3. चतुर्थक (व्हाइट-कॉलर)
4. पंचम (गोल्ड-कॉलर)
सूची-II:
(a) वरिष्ठ नीति-निर्माता एवं कॉर्पोरेट CEO
(b) अनुसंधान, सॉफ्टवेयर एवं सूचना विश्लेषण
(c) इस्पात प्रगलन एवं वस्त्र निर्माण
(d) मत्स्य पालन, खनन एवं वानिकी
e:
Primary = extraction/harvesting (d); Secondary = manufacturing (c); Quaternary = knowledge/R&D/IT (b); Quinary = top-level decision-making/gold-collar (a) (1-d, 2-c, 3-b, 4-a)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Tertiary sector (Pink-collar/Services) includes retail, transport, banking, tourism, and teaching.
2. Footloose industries (e.g., electronics, watch-making, software) are NOT bound to raw material locations and can be set up anywhere with good connectivity.
3. Trans-Siberian Railway (Moscow to Vladivostok, ~9,289 km) is the world's longest continuous railway line.
qe:
Match List-I (Economic Activity Sector) with List-II (Example) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Primary (Red-collar)
2. Secondary (Blue-collar)
3. Quaternary (White-collar)
4. Quinary (Gold-collar)
List-II:
(a) Senior government policy-makers & corporate CEOs
(b) R&D, software & information analytics
(c) Steel smelting & textile manufacturing
(d) Fishing, mining & forestry

q: कोयले की किस किस्म में कार्बन की मात्रा सर्वाधिक (80%–95%) होती है और जो न्यूनतम धुएँ व नीली लौ के साथ जलता है?
e:
Anthracite is the highest-grade metamorphic coal (80%–95% carbon); in India it is found in small quantities only in Jammu & Kashmir (Kalakote) (एंथ्रासाइट सर्वोत्तम कोटि का कोयला है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Coal quality order (highest to lowest): Anthracite → Bituminous → Lignite (Brown coal, Neyveli in Tamil Nadu) → Peat.
2. About 98% of India's coal reserves are Gondwana (Bituminous) coal found in Damodar, Son, Mahanadi, and Godavari valleys (Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro, Talcher, Korba, Singrauli).
3. Raniganj (West Bengal) is India's oldest coalfield; Jharia (Jharkhand) is famous for coking coal.
qe: Which variety of coal has the highest carbon content (80%–95%) and burns cleanly with a blue flame and minimal smoke?

q: अल्फ्रेड वेबर के औद्योगिक अवस्थिति सिद्धांत में 'आइसोडापेन' (Isodapane) क्या है?
o: A line joining points of equal raw material quality
A line joining points of equal total transportation cost (sum of raw material and finished product transport costs)
A line joining points of equal labour wages
A line joining points of equal market demand
e:
An Isodapane connects locations having equal TOTAL transport cost (whereas an Isotim connects points of equal transport cost for a single input/product); the 'Critical Isodapane' determines whether cheap labour or agglomeration pulls an industry away from the minimum-transport-cost point (आइसोडापेन समान कुल परिवहन लागत वाले बिंदुओं को मिलाने वाली रेखा है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. August Lösch (1940) proposed the 'Profit Maximization' (Market Area) theory of industrial location as a counterpoint to Weber's least-cost model.
2. Walter Isard founded Regional Science, integrating location theory and spatial economics.
3. David Smith developed 'Spatial Margins of Profitability'.
qe: In Alfred Weber's Industrial Location Theory, what is an 'Isodapane' (आइसोडापेन)?
oe: A line joining points of equal raw material quality
A line joining points of equal total transportation cost (sum of raw material and finished product transport costs)
A line joining points of equal labour wages
A line joining points of equal market demand

q: विश्व के सबसे बड़े मत्स्य ग्रहण क्षेत्र (जैसे न्यूफाउंडलैंड के पास ग्रैंड बैंक और उत्तरी सागर में डॉगर बैंक) मुख्यतः किस महासागरीय क्षेत्र में पाए जाते हैं?
e:
Wide, sunlit, shallow Continental Shelves (<200 m deep) enriched by upwelling and convergence of warm & cold currents promote abundant plankton growth, supporting massive fish populations (उथले महाद्वीपीय मग्नतट पर प्लवक की प्रचुरता से विशाल मत्स्य क्षेत्र बनते हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Continental Shelf also holds major offshore petroleum and natural gas reserves (e.g., Mumbai High, North Sea).
2. Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep, ~11,034 m in Western Pacific) is the deepest point in the world's oceans.
3. Mid-Atlantic Ridge is the longest underwater mountain chain formed by divergent plate boundaries.
qe: The world's largest fishing grounds (such as Grand Banks off Newfoundland and Dogger Bank in the North Sea) are predominantly found in which oceanic zone?
oe: Wide, shallow Continental Shelves where warm and cold currents meet

q: भारत की सबसे प्राचीन वलित पर्वत शृंखला कौन-सी है, जो गुजरात से राजस्थान होते हुए दिल्ली तक फैली हुई है?
e:
The Aravalli Range (Precambrian era, now a residual/relict mountain) is India's oldest fold mountain; its highest peak is Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) on Mount Abu, Rajasthan (अरावली भारत की सबसे प्राचीन वलित पर्वत श्रेणी है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates; three parallel ranges: Himadri (Greater), Himachal (Lesser), and Shiwalik (Outer).
2. Satpura is a Block Mountain (Horst) flanked by Narmada and Tapi rift valleys; its highest peak is Dhupgarh (1,350 m, Panchmarhi).
3. Nilgiri Hills (highest peak Doddabetta, 2,637 m) mark the junction of the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.
qe: Which mountain range is the oldest fold mountain system in India, extending from Gujarat through Rajasthan to Delhi?

q: उत्तराखंड के किस पवित्र संगम पर अलकनंदा और भागीरथी नदियाँ मिलकर गंगा नदी का निर्माण करती हैं?
e:
Bhagirathi (originating from Gangotri/Gaumukh) and Alaknanda (Satopanth glacier) unite at Devprayag to become the Ganga (देवप्रयाग में भागीरथी व अलकनंदा के संगम से गंगा बनती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Panch Prayag (north to south): Vishnuprayag (Alaknanda + Dhauliganga), Nandaprayag (+ Nandakini), Karnaprayag (+ Pindar), Rudraprayag (+ Mandakini), Devprayag (+ Bhagirathi).
2. Ganga enters the plains at Haridwar and flows 2,525 km across 5 Indian states (Uttarakhand, UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal) into the Bay of Bengal.
3. Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo in Tibet, Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, Brahmaputra in Assam, and Jamuna in Bangladesh.
qe: At which sacred confluence in Uttarakhand do the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi rivers meet to form the River Ganga?

q: भारत का कौन-सा तटीय राज्य अपनी वार्षिक वर्षा का अधिकांश भाग शीतकाल (अक्टूबर–दिसंबर) में लौटते हुए / उत्तर-पूर्वी मानसून से प्राप्त करता है?
e:
Tamil Nadu's Coromandel Coast lies in the rain-shadow of the Western Ghats during the Southwest Monsoon and receives ~50%–60% of its rainfall from the Northeast Monsoon picking up moisture over the Bay of Bengal (तमिलनाडु का कोरोमंडल तट लौटते मानसून से शीतकालीन वर्षा प्राप्त करता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Northwestern India (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP) receives winter rainfall from 'Western Disturbances' (temperate cyclones from the Mediterranean Sea), beneficial for Rabi wheat.
2. Pre-monsoon showers: 'Mango Showers' (Kerala/Karnataka), 'Cherry Blossom / Coffee Showers' (Karnataka), 'Kal Baisakhi / Nor'westers' (Bengal/Assam).
3. Mawsynram (Meghalaya, Khasi Hills) receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world (~11,872 mm).
qe: Which coastal state of India receives the bulk of its annual rainfall during winter (October–December) from the Retreating / Northeast Monsoon?

q:
सूची-I (प्रमुख बाँध परियोजना) को सूची-II (नदी) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. हीराकुंड बाँध
2. भाखड़ा नांगल बाँध
3. टिहरी बाँध
4. नागार्जुन सागर बाँध
सूची-II:
(a) कृष्णा
(b) भागीरथी
(c) सतलुज
(d) महानदी
e:
Hirakud (Odisha, longest dam in India) is on Mahanadi; Bhakra Nangal (HP/Punjab) on Sutlej; Tehri (Uttarakhand, highest dam in India, ~260.5 m) on Bhagirathi; Nagarjuna Sagar (Telangana/AP) on Krishna (1-d, 2-c, 3-b, 4-a)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC, 1948) was independent India's first multipurpose river valley project (modelled on Tennessee Valley Authority, USA).
2. Jawaharlal Nehru famously called multipurpose dams the 'Temples of Modern India'.
3. Idukki Dam (Kerala, arch dam) is on Periyar river; Mettur Dam (Tamil Nadu) is on Kaveri river.
qe:
Match List-I (Major Dam / Hydro Project in India) with List-II (River) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Hirakud Dam
2. Bhakra Nangal Dam
3. Tehri Dam
4. Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
List-II:
(a) Krishna
(b) Bhagirathi
(c) Sutlej
(d) Mahanadi

q: भारत के सर्वाधिक भौगोलिक क्षेत्रफल में किस प्रकार के प्राकृतिक वन (सागौन, साल, शीशम और चंदन युक्त) फैले हुए हैं?
e:
Tropical Deciduous Forests (Moist: 100–200 cm rainfall; Dry: 70–100 cm rainfall) are the most widespread forests in India (~65% of forest cover) (उष्णकटिबंधीय पर्णपाती वन भारत में सर्वाधिक विस्तृत हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Sundarbans (West Bengal, Ganga-Brahmaputra delta) is the world's largest mangrove forest, named after the 'Sundari' tree (Heritiera fomes).
2. Tropical Evergreen forests occur where rainfall exceeds 200 cm (Western Ghats, Andaman & Nicobar, NE India — Rosewood, Mahogany, Ebony).
3. As per India State of Forest Report (ISFR), Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest area, while Mizoram has the highest forest cover percentage.
qe: Which type of natural forest covers the largest geographical area in India (featuring Teak, Sal, Shisham, and Sandalwood)?

q: बंगाल की खाड़ी में कौन-सा संकीर्ण जल चैनल अंडमान द्वीप समूह को निकोबार द्वीप समूह से अलग करता है?
e:
The Ten Degree Channel (10° N latitude) separates Little Andaman from Car Nicobar (10° चैनल अंडमान को निकोबार से अलग करता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy (India) from Maldives; Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the rest of Lakshadweep.
2. Duncan Passage separates South Andaman from Little Andaman; Coco Channel separates North Andaman from Myanmar's Coco Islands.
3. Barren Island (Andaman Sea) is India's only active volcano.
qe: Which narrow water channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal?

q: भारत का कौन-सा राज्य लौह अयस्क (मयूरभंज, क्योंझर और सुंदरगढ़ खदानों सहित), बॉक्साइट और क्रोमाइट का अग्रणी उत्पादक है?
e:
Odisha is India's #1 producer of Iron Ore, Bauxite, Chromite, and Manganese (ओडिशा लौह अयस्क, बॉक्साइट और क्रोमाइट उत्पादन में प्रथम है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Other major iron ore mines: Bailadila (Chhattisgarh), Kudremukh & Bellary (Karnataka), Singhbhum/Noamundi (Jharkhand).
2. Khetri (Rajasthan) and Malanjkhand (MP) are famous for Copper; Jaduguda (Jharkhand) for Uranium; Kolar & Hutti (Karnataka) for Gold.
3. Digboi (Assam, 1901) is India's oldest oil refinery; Mumbai High is India's largest offshore oilfield.
qe: Which Indian state is the leading producer of Iron Ore (housing famous mines like Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, and Sundargarh) as well as Bauxite and Chromite?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी एक प्रमुख रबी फसल है जिसे उत्तर भारत में अक्टूबर–दिसंबर में बोया जाता है और मार्च–अप्रैल में काटा जाता है?
e:
Wheat, Barley, Gram, Peas, and Mustard are major Rabi (winter) crops, whereas Rice, Maize, Jowar, Bajra, Cotton, Jute, and Groundnut are Kharif (monsoon) crops (गेहूँ प्रमुख रबी फसल है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Zaid crops (March–June) include Watermelon, Muskmelon, Cucumber, and Fodder crops.
2. India's Green Revolution (mid-1960s) had its greatest impact on Wheat and Rice in Punjab, Haryana, and Western UP.
3. National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) is at Cuttack (Odisha); Indian Institute of Wheat & Barley Research is at Karnal (Haryana).
qe: Which of the following is a major Rabi crop sown in October–December and harvested in March–April in North India?

q: प्रयागराज से हल्दिया तक 1,620 किमी लंबा भारत का सबसे लंबा राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग (NW-1) किस नदी प्रणाली पर स्थित है?
e:
National Waterway-1 (NW-1, 1,620 km, Prayagraj to Haldia) runs along the Ganga–Bhagirathi–Hooghly river system across UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal (NW-1 गंगा-भागीरथी-हुगली प्रणाली पर स्थित है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. NW-2 is on the Brahmaputra (Sadiya–Dhubri, 891 km, Assam); NW-3 is the West Coast Canal (Kerala).
2. Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI, est. 1986) is headquartered in Noida, Uttar Pradesh.
3. National Highway 44 (NH-44, Srinagar to Kanyakumari, ~3,745 km) is India's longest National Highway.
qe: Which is India's longest National Waterway (NW-1), stretching 1,620 km from Prayagraj to Haldia?

q: भारत का कौन-सा प्रमुख बंदरगाह गुजरात के कच्छ की खाड़ी में स्थित एक ज्वारीय बंदरगाह है (दीनदयाल बंदरगाह के रूप में पुनर्नामित), जिसे विभाजन के बाद मुंबई बंदरगाह का दबाव कम करने हेतु विकसित किया गया?
e:
Kandla (Deendayal Port, Gujarat) is a tidal port and Asia's first Export Processing Zone (1965), built to compensate for the loss of Karachi Port after 1947 (कांडला एक ज्वारीय बंदरगाह है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. India has 13 Major Ports (12 public + Ennore/Kamarajar corporate); Visakhapatnam (AP) is India's deepest landlocked natural port.
2. Nhava Sheva / Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT, Maharashtra) is India's largest container port.
3. Kolkata/Haldia (Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port) is India's only major riverine port.
qe: Which major port of India is a tidal port located in the Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat), renamed Deendayal Port, developed after Partition to ease pressure on Mumbai Port?

q: कश्मीर घाटी के करेवा निक्षेपों (प्लीस्टोसीन युग के सरोवरीय निक्षेप) में भारत की किस उच्च-मूल्य नकदी फसल की विशिष्ट खेती की जाती है?
e:
Karewas (thick glacial-clay and lacustrine silt terraces in Kashmir Valley, especially Pampore) are famous for cultivating GI-tagged Kashmiri Saffron (Zafran) and almonds (करेवा मिट्टी केसर की खेती के लिए विश्व प्रसिद्ध है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Duars (in Bengal/Assam foothills) are fertile alluvial formations ideal for tea gardens.
2. Bhabar (pebble belt where rivers disappear), Terai (marshy re-emergence zone), Bhangar (old alluvium), and Khadar (new alluvium) are the four physiographic belts of the Northern Plains.
3. Kashmir Saffron received its Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2020.
qe: In the Karewa formations of the Kashmir Valley (lacustrine deposits of Pleistocene origin), which high-value cash crop is uniquely cultivated in India?

q: भारत के निम्नलिखित लौह एवं इस्पात संयंत्रों में से किसकी स्थापना 1907 में निजी क्षेत्र में साकची (जमशेदपुर) में स्वर्णरेखा और खरकई नदियों के संगम पर की गई थी?
e:
TISCO (now Tata Steel) was founded by Jamsetji Tata in 1907 at Jamshedpur (Jharkhand) with ideal access to Noamundi iron ore, Jharia coal, and Subarnarekha water (TISCO की स्थापना 1907 में जमशेदपुर में हुई थी)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Second Five-Year Plan public sector plants: Bhilai (Chhattisgarh — USSR), Rourkela (Odisha — West Germany), Durgapur (West Bengal — UK).
2. Third Plan: Bokaro (Jharkhand — USSR); Fourth Plan: Salem (TN), Visakhapatnam (AP — India's first shore-based steel plant), Vijayanagar (Karnataka).
3. SAIL (Steel Authority of India Limited) was incorporated in 1973.
qe: Which of the following Iron and Steel plants in India was established in the private sector in 1907 at Sakchi (Jamshedpur) at the confluence of the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा पर्वतीय दर्रा जास्कर/वृहद हिमालय श्रेणी के पार श्रीनगर को लेह से जोड़ता है?
e:
Zoji La Pass (Ladakh/J&K) links Srinagar (Kashmir Valley) with Kargil and Leh (जोजिला दर्रा श्रीनगर को लेह से जोड़ता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Banihal Pass (Pir Panjal range, Jawahar Tunnel) connects Jammu to Srinagar.
2. Rohtang Pass (Atal Tunnel, 9.02 km) connects Kullu Valley to Lahaul-Spiti in Himachal Pradesh.
3. Nathu La & Jelep La are in Sikkim; Bomdi La & Diphu Pass are in Arunachal Pradesh; Palghat (Palakkad Gap) connects Kerala to Tamil Nadu.
qe: Which of the following mountain passes correctly connects Srinagar to Leh across the Zaskar / Great Himalayan range?

q: भारत पर लागू कोपेन के जलवायु वर्गीकरण के अनुसार, उत्तर का विशाल मैदान (उत्तर प्रदेश और बिहार के अधिकांश भाग सहित) किस जलवायु प्रकार के अंतर्गत आता है?
e:
In Köppen's classification for India, 'Cwg' (Monsoon type with dry winters and hot summers) covers the Ganga Plains, Eastern Rajasthan, Northern MP, and most of Uttar Pradesh & Bihar (उत्तर प्रदेश व गंगा का मैदान कोपेन के 'Cwg' वर्ग में आता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Amw = Monsoon with short dry winter (Malabar/Konkan West Coast); As = Monsoon with dry summer (Coromandel Coast / Tamil Nadu).
2. Aw = Tropical Savanna (most of Peninsular Plateau); BWhw = Hot Desert (Western Rajasthan / Thar); BShw = Semi-arid Steppe.
3. E = Polar/Alpine type (Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal, and Uttarakhand high Himalayas).
qe: According to the Koppen climatic classification applied to India, the Great Northern Plains (including most of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar) fall under which climatic type?
